summary.name: ParrotFlow
summary.one_liner: ParrotFlow is a free, open-source, programmable local dictation app for macOS that spells names, code and shorthand the way you define in rules, scripts and vocabulary.
use_cases: dictating bug reports and notes on a Mac
turning spoken names and handles into correct spelling
converting spoken PR numbers into GitHub links
running custom text-processing scripts on dictated speech
summary.what_it_does: ParrotFlow dictates speech into text on macOS and lets you shape the output with rules, scripts and a custom vocabulary. Rules can map phrases to outputs, for example turning a spoken name into an @handle or a spoken PR number into a #478 link. Steps can be chained in a fixed pipeline, and any script that reads and writes text can be a step. Prompt steps can be bound to keys or pill buttons, and they use a language model only when one is configured, either local via Ollama or in the cloud. The page also describes a ParrotFlow skill that a coding agent can use to write rules and check the config.
notable: Rules, scripts and vocabulary are readable and editable, so every transformation is visible
Pipeline of ordered steps, with prompt steps bound to keys or pill buttons
Small local models (mmBERT, Qwen3 0.6B, spaCy) edit the raw transcript without a language model
Coding agent skill can write dictation rules from plain-English descriptions
caveats: Needs about 2 GB of disk and 1 GB of memory
Prompt steps need a language model, which can be local via Ollama or a cloud model
